actions.text: Committee on Indian Affairs. Hearings held.
Read twice and referred to the Committee on Indian Affairs. (Sponsor introductory remarks on measure: CR S1011)

dimensions.assessment: Directly affects the Pechanga Band of Indians and local management jurisdictions in Riverside County, California.
dimensions.evidence: takes approximately 860 acres of land in Riverside County, California, into trust for the benefit of the Pechanga Band of Indians.

dimensions.assessment: Changes the legal status of 860 acres of federal land into tribal trust land, restricting its use permanently to open space and conservation, while barring gaming.
dimensions.evidence: The land taken into trust under subsection (a) shall be... maintained as open space... [and] shall not be used for any class II gaming or class III gaming

dimensions.assessment: No significant federal spending, revenue changes, or economic effects are specified or implied beyond administrative land transfer.
A localized land-in-trust transfer for a single specific Indian Tribe with designated land use conditions.
dimensions.evidence: the covered land is hereby taken into trust for the benefit of the Tribe.

dimensions.assessment: Permanent change in land status and trust administration.
dimensions.evidence: administered in accordance with the laws and regulations generally applicable to property held in trust by the United States

missing_information: Specific economic or administrative cost estimates for transferring the land are not provided.
importance_detail.rationale: Takes approximately 860 acres of land in Riverside County, California, into trust for the Pechanga Band of Indians. The effects are geographically localized to the specified parcel and tribe.
